method.input: Puppeteer Edge mouse.move, native pointer lock; no pointerLockElement shim or __cmd.turn
method.fixture: In-memory independent HTML route imports original main.ts; World.step captures World/Ship and only updates real turrets, freezing ship physics and AI. Original frame/input/render/viewport retained.
method.horizon: Actual camera geometric sea horizon at screen centre X, projected at infinity (not a HUD line or pixel-segmented haze boundary).
method.seaPoint: A fixed world-space mean-sea-level point, selected once per view at baseline; never follows aim.
method.frames: Controlled RAF, 50 ms steps; all original frame/input/camera updates retained, renderer instance skips intermediate draws and renders the final state once per batch. SwiftShader, no performance benchmark.
method.mousePackets: Each displacement uses 15 genuine mouse.move steps. A single 300px packet can clamp range to 250m and produce incidental large pitch; do not confuse that edge case with working pitch control.
method.setup: ONLY scene initialization after native lock warp: __cmd.aimAt(player.x, player.z+9000), then settle 24 real frames. All aiming thereafter uses trusted native mouse; no aimAt/turn/zoom/fire debug shortcuts.
method.readiness: Runtime readiness fixture sets forward turret reload=0 and disables aft reload; no 30s wait, no mocked fire. Native original World.step(dt,false) advances actual shells without rendering; ship physics temporarily frozen during flight.

recommendedFix: Investigate real Shift/C sea-point drift: requestAimSync uses a fixed .65s window while camera position/anchor and visible wave height continue to change; preserve the world aim point until the camera transition actually settles.

Investigate locked 1px vertical input: aimSurfaceHit can intersect foreground island terrain far short of the locked target and create excessive offRange, immediately breaking lock. Keep small vertical trim effective without losing target lock; retain intentional large-input release.
Do not reintroduce range-only vertical acceptance: require actual camera direction, projected world/horizon movement, real sea projection and physical shell impacts.
